skill.name: pattern-detection
skill.description: Detect recurring code, security, data, and trend patterns using read-only searches, regex checks, and simple statistical examples.
skill.summary: Find code smells, vulnerability patterns, duplicate structures, sensitive data markers, and data anomalies with read-only analysis.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and read-only search examples. The hard-coded URLs are reference links, and the API-key pattern is a regex used to detect hard-coded secrets, not secret access. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, file modification, or runtime network behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples resemble executable shell instructions to static scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that the snippets are optional read-only searches or convert them to Grep-tool workflow steps.

remediation.issue: Secret scanning examples can reveal sensitive values if results are pasted into chat.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to report file and line references only and avoid sharing secret values.

content.value_statement: Teams miss recurring defects, risky patterns, and data anomalies when reviews rely only on manual inspection. This skill guides read-only pattern searches, regex checks, and concise reports for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Identifies code smell patterns such as long functions, magic numbers, TODO markers, and empty error handlers.
Searches for security indicators including SQL concatenation, hard-coded secret patterns, eval calls, and unsafe innerHTML assignments.
Uses regex examples to count sensitive data formats such as email addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, credit cards, and SSNs.
Demonstrates z-score, IQR, moving average, growth, and volatility checks for anomaly and trend analysis.
Produces a severity-based pattern detection report with files, lines, descriptions, and recommended actions.
limitations: A match is not proof of a defect; reviewers must inspect surrounding context.
The skill does not modify code or apply automated fixes.
Shell snippets are examples and may need adaptation for each repository.
Statistical examples require suitable numeric data and Python packages when used outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Review risky code patterns
use_cases.description: Scan a repository for common vulnerability indicators and produce a prioritized review list.

use_cases.title: Find refactoring candidates
use_cases.description: Locate long functions, duplicate patterns, magic numbers, and unfinished work before a cleanup sprint.

use_cases.title: Monitor data trends
use_cases.description: Inspect time-series metrics for outliers, moving averages, growth direction, and volatility changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find basic code smells
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pattern-detection to scan this repository for TODO markers, magic numbers, empty error handlers, and long functions. Report files, lines, severity, and suggested next checks.

prompt_templates.title: Check security indicators
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pattern-detection to find SQL concatenation, hard-coded secret patterns, eval or exec usage, and unsafe innerHTML assignments. Separate likely issues from matches that need context.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze data anomalies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pattern-detection on the provided metric data. Identify outliers, trend direction, moving average changes, growth rate, and volatility. Explain which findings need validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a detection plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pattern-detection to design a staged review plan for this repository and dataset. Include regex checks, structural checks, anomaly methods, priorities, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Scan a TypeScript service for unsafe DOM updates and hard-coded credential indicators.
output: High severity: possible credential pattern found in a configuration sample. Confirm whether the value is test-only.
Medium severity: repeated direct innerHTML assignment pattern. Review sanitization and trusted content boundaries.
Recommended action: verify each match before filing defects.

output_examples.input: Review a Python service for maintainability patterns before refactoring.
output: Medium severity: several functions appear longer than the project standard and need local context review.
Low severity: repeated TODO and FIXME markers suggest unfinished cleanup work.
Recommended action: group matches by module owner and prioritize high-change files.

output_examples.input: Analyze daily transaction counts for unexpected changes.
output: Outlier: one day exceeds the z-score threshold and should be compared with release and incident records.
Trend: the seven-day average is above the thirty-day average, indicating short-term growth.
Recommended action: validate source data quality before making operational decisions.

best_practices: Start with a focused pattern set and expand after verifying initial matches.
Always review surrounding code before assigning severity.
Keep reports concise and separate security, maintainability, and data findings.
anti_patterns: Treating every regex match as a confirmed vulnerability without context.
Running broad scans that expose sensitive results in logs or chat.
Mixing unrelated pattern types in one report without priority or severity.

faq.question: Does this skill change files?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for read-only analysis and reporting.

faq.question: Does it find every vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. It finds indicators that need human review and context validation.

faq.question: Which tools does it use?
faq.answer: It is designed around read-only file inspection and grep-style search workflows.

faq.question: Can it analyze data trends?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for outliers, moving averages, growth, and volatility.

faq.question: How should I handle possible secrets?
faq.answer: Do not paste secret values. Report file and line references, then rotate confirmed credentials by policy.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
